## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: One 🚨 BLOCKING: the PR introduces a deterministic test failure — `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart:351` still asserts the pre-gh-2096 mechanism (`budgetSource.token.isCancelled == true`), which the per-call token change intentionally inverted; reproduced on the branch (1050/1 in compaction+agent) and verified green on `origin/main`. The engine work itself is sound: analyzer clean, judge_health latch/probe/diagnosis logic correct and additive, old sessions stay byte-identical, docs + CHANGELOG present.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 [comment1](pr_review_comments/comment1.md) — stale #515 assertion contradicts the PR's own new test; CI red, must fix before merge.
- 💡 Digest: `engine.dart:574-578` — a successful probe's judged hide pass carries `judgeLatched: false`; the field doc promises the flag on "a probe receipt", so hosts can't distinguish probe-driven successes.
- 💡 Digest: `engine.dart:173` — `judgeProbeAfter` has no config surface (`compaction.judgeProbeAfterSeconds`); CHANGELOG reads "default 10 min" as if configurable, but it is a constructor param only.
- 💡 Digest: `engine.dart:730-748` — the latched skip emits kind `'hide'` with `ok: false`; a deliberate skip reads as a failure in hosts counting `!ok` passes — a dedicated kind (`'hide-skip'`) would be cleaner.
- 🪶 Digest: `judge_health.dart:86-97` — a latched record with null `target` never gets the class-change probe bypass (unreachable via real writers, defensive note only).
- 🪶 Digest: `structured_judge_fallback_test.dart:229` — the regex hardcodes `~104 tok`, brittle to unrelated ledger-line format changes.

**Next Steps**:
1. Update the stale assertion in `auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart` to gh-2096 semantics (per-call token cancelled; run-wide token stays live) — then re-run the three verify commands from the PR description.

🚨 severity: BLOCKING —
🚨 **BLOCKING: stale #515 assertion — this PR introduces a deterministic test failure (CI breakage)**

The per-call token change is the point of gh-2096, but the pre-existing test whose body asserts the OLD mechanism (this hunk's test — the stale assertion sits at line 351, ~14 lines below the changed line) was not updated:

```dart
// The engine killed the in-flight call at the token, not just the
// await: the provider layer sees the abort (#515 semantics kept).
expect(budgetSource.token.isCancelled, isTrue);   // line 351
```

On this branch the judge timeout cancels ONLY the per-call child token, so `budgetSource.token` stays live and the assertion fails:

- Reproduced twice on the PR branch: `dart test test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart --plain-name "the hide judge budget kill"` → `Expected: true / Actual: <false>` at `351:5`. The full `test/compaction + test/agent` sweep is **1050 passed / 1 failed — this is the only failure**.
- Verified **passing on `origin/main`** in a clean worktree — the failure is introduced by this PR, deterministic, not flaky.
- This PR's own new test asserts the **opposite** semantics (`structured_judge_health_test.dart`: `expect(budgetSource.token.isCancelled, isFalse, reason: 'a judge timeout must not cancel the run-wide budget token')`) — the two tests now encode contradictory behavior, and the old one loses.

Fix: update this test to gh-2096 semantics — assert the **per-call token** was cancelled (the provider layer still sees the abort; #515 is preserved via the forwarded child token) and the **run-wide budget token stayed live**. The engine code itself is correct; only this stale assertion needs the update.
